summary: An Iterator hands out values one at a time with hasNext() and next(). A class that implements Iterable<T> can be used in an enhanced for loop.
notes: iterator() returns a new Iterator each time it is called, so the same Countdown can be looped over more than once.
return current--; returns the current value and then subtracts 1.
next() throws NoSuchElementException when there are no values left. That is the rule for every Java Iterator.
pitfall: Implementing Iterator<Integer> but not Iterable<Integer> makes for (int n : new Countdown(5)) fail to compile with for-each not applicable to expression type.
